subject: maths
question: A man purchases a certain number of identical calculators at a rate of ₹1,200 per dozen. He sells them at ₹110 per piece. Find how many calculators he bought if his total profit is ₹360.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit per **dozen** = (**Selling Price** per piece × 12) − **Cost Price** per dozen

⇒ Profit per dozen = (110 × 12) − 1200 = 1320 − 1200 = ₹120

Total items in **dozens** = **Total Profit** ÷ Profit per dozen = 360 ÷ 120 = 3 **dozens**

Total number of **calculators** = 3 × 12 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 calculators.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price** (CP) of 1 dozen (12 calculators) = ₹1,200

**Selling Price** (SP) of 1 calculator = ₹110

**Total Profit** = ₹360

**Formula Used:**

1. **Profit** per unit = **Selling Price** per unit − **Cost Price** per unit

2. Number of units = **Total Profit** ÷ **Profit** per unit

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11aba4b9e43b74c680f3faac83e09dc66e913855d6745a8ad88038d3ae70391d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Cost Price** (CP) of 1 calculator = 1200 ÷ 12 = ₹100

⇒ **Selling Price** (SP) of 1 calculator = ₹110

⇒ **Profit** on 1 calculator = 110 − 100 = ₹10

⇒ Number of **calculators** bought = 360 ÷ 10

⇒ Number of **calculators** = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 calculators.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100. In this case, Profit % = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit %) ÷ 100. This is used to find the **Selling Price** when CP and profit percentage are known.

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Always convert given quantities (like dozens, gross, or score) into **single units** to simplify the calculation of profit or loss per item.
